elements.element: No punitive/penalty rate applied to amounts payable by Customer (e.g., multiplier on late-payment interest)
elements.evidence: Operation replaced "three hundred percent (300%) of the rate described in Subparagraph 7.8" with "the rate described in Subparagraph 7.8"; charges now accrue at the compensatory 7.8 rate.

elements.element: No liquidated damages amount stipulated as payable by Customer
elements.evidence: Neither 7.9 nor 23.2 stipulates any pre-agreed damages sum payable by Customer; 23.2 preserves only "the payment of its unpaid accounts, which have been incurred prior to the actual reclamation."

elements.element: No other penalty borne by Customer on default (forfeiture of paid amounts / loss of assigned capacity without payment or credit)
elements.evidence: Untouched 23.2: "the defaulting Party shall not be entitled to any payment or credit for the reclaimed capacity" and "is not entitled to any reimbursement of any amounts it had paid under this Agreement."

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: Condition absent — no early-termination fee is imposed anywhere in 7.9 or 23.2, so no cap is required.

elements.element: That fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer
elements.evidence: No liquidated sum is payable by Customer; late-payment charges are now compensatory ("computed at the rate described in Subparagraph 7.8") and 23.2 preserves only actual "unpaid accounts."

reasons: The single surgical replacement removes the 300% punitive multiplier so late-payment charges accrue at the compensatory Subparagraph 7.8 rate — this cures the clearest penalty payable by us and is the minimum change needed (an operator/number-level edit, no rewrite).

Preferred is not fully achieved: Subparagraph 23.2 is untouched and still imposes penal forfeiture on the defaulting (potentially our) Party — no "payment or credit for the reclaimed capacity" and no "reimbursement of any amounts it had paid" — which is a penalty borne by us rather than compensation for actual loss.
Fallback is satisfied on its material terms: there is no early-termination fee and no stipulated liquidated amount payable by us, so the capped-fee condition is demonstrably absent.

Suggested follow-on if the preferred level is required: add to 23.2 that on reclamation the defaulting Party receives a pro-rata credit or refund of prepaid amounts for capacity not received, so the remedy is compensatory rather than punitive.
No unrelated commercial terms were disturbed; the highest-lawful-rate savings language and the definition of "paid" remain effective, and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference was introduced.
